research_question: Can a standards-linked, role-aware entropy boundary prevent a rollback in the origin PQ component from deterministically removing freshness from the independent peer component in hybrid or dual-PQC key establishment?

hypotheses.H1: Shared state, label-only derivation, and an unreachable split sham do not preserve peer freshness under origin RNG-state reuse.
hypotheses.H2: A reached role-routed entropy boundary preserves peer freshness while the deliberately rolled-back origin component repeats.
hypotheses.H3: An RFC-8937-style hedge preserves origin, peer, and combined freshness under raw-state reuse when unique context survives, but fails when raw state and context are both reset.
hypotheses.H4: The qualitative decision surface transfers across a real Go TLS ClientHello path, RustCrypto X-Wing, and a liboqs ML-KEM-768 plus HQC-3 dual-PQC realization.

implementations.role_mapping: audited tls.Config.Rand call order; experiment-only, not a production API recommendation

sample_design.unit_isolation: one child process per matched pair
sample_design.schedule: deterministic randomized permutation persisted before execution
sample_design.persistence: one canonical JSON line, flush, and fsync per completed unit

analysis.primary: exact matched response-surface assertions against pre-frozen expectations
analysis.statistics: no population-prevalence inference; counts are deterministic implementation observations
analysis.replay: complete semantic replay under an independently permuted schedule
analysis.timing: recorded only for diagnostics and excluded from claims

failure_criteria: any unit differs from the frozen qualitative expectation
any expected architecture or recipe cell is incomplete
any source, binary, schedule, record, or summary hash is missing
replay differs semantically after excluding timing and schedule position
a claimed split is not reached at the actual randomness interface
claim_exclusions: submission readiness before all gates pass
